$doc: Tile streaming, in world units.
The page stays the unit of transfer and storage: one PostGIS query and bake
on the API side, one ~4MB decode, one `tile_map` key, one eviction. What is
derived rather than chosen is *which* pages: the nearest RESIDENT_PAGES to
the view anchor (module/world/frame/range.ts's pages_to_hold), which is at
once what gets fetched and what stays decoded. One set, so a page can never
be requested and then dropped from under its own in-flight request.
How many pages stay decoded at most: the nearest this many, and the rest
are dropped. A count, not a radius, because the thing worth bounding is
memory — one decoded page is ~4MB and a tab has been lost to holding too
many — and a count bounds it directly at any zoom or range.
It has to be comfortably more than the ~21 the range itself fetches, or
panning out of a page and back refetches it, and a page with no tile is
not merely coarse: it is not mounted at all, so its whole square vanishes
at once. 32 pages is ~129MB, against the 49 (~197MB) that discarded the
tab on an iPhone 13 mini and the 9 (~36MB) the old fetch window held.
Never more than the core memory's page section holds, less PAGE_MARGIN.
Pages a release keeps for its quarantine (resident.ts) while the next
ones arrive, and the shared ocean page.
How far to look when picking those pages. Only wide enough that the
nearest RESIDENT_PAGES are always available to pick (39 at worst), since
the count is what actually decides; a page beyond this is further than
the 32nd nearest can ever be.
